rv.q: Under Megumi Nakamura's direction, Sulfur Bottom blurs time, memory, and reality intriguingly, allowing the family to communicate with each other beyond the grave.
But Varma’s complicated storytelling doesn’t serve the play’s mission to call attention to environmental injustice.
Rishi Varma’s Sulfur Bottom has its heart in the right place but its complicated and confused storytelling makes this new play difficult to follow.
Your mind may be so stimulated that you’ll swear you can smell the sulfured air of the industrial complex in the theatre.
Sulfur Bottom’s non-Equity actors hit some nice emotional beats and generally perform well enough.

cn.t: Varma's climate parable about a family on poisoned land earns praise for its emotional resonance over preachiness, but critics find the storytelling confusing, with unclear flashbacks and structural complexity that muddles its environmental justice message.

vr.q: While I thought the show was at times disjointed or confusing, it was certainly thematically interesting.
